identity.title: Inefficient jet-induced star formation in Centaurus A. High resolution ALMA observations of the northern filaments

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper, we present recent ALMA observations of the $^{12}CO$(1-0) line along the northern filaments of Centaurus A.

evidence.quote: At the distance of Centaurus A (3.8 Mpc, $1''\sim 18.3\: pc$; (cite: Harris_2010))

question.value: Why does molecular gas in the northern filaments of Centaurus A not follow the Kennicutt-Schmidt law, and does the eastern CO bright region differ from the rest of the filaments?

evidence.quote: The goal of this paper is to understand why the molecular gas in the northern filaments of Centaurus A does not follow the Kennicutt-Schmidt law, and whether there is a difference between the eastern CO bright region and the rest of the filaments.
using Band 3 receivers (project ADS/JAO.ALMA$\#$2015.1.01019.S)
during Cycle 3 using Band 3 receivers
We mapped the $^{12}CO$(1-0) emission in the northern filaments of Centaurus A
consists in a mosaic of 34 pointings, each with an integration time between 140 and 430s.
The baselines ranged from 15 m to 704 m
providing a resolution of $1.30''\times 0.99''$ ($PA=81.5$$^{\circ}$)
The largest angular scale recovered by the interferometer is $14''$

findings_qualitative.value: Clouds have size, sigma_v and mass similar to Milky Way clouds but higher virial parameters; the Horseshoe complex is shock-excited and shows no star formation

evidence.quote: These clouds have size, velocity dispersion, and mass of the same order than molecular clouds in the Milky Way.

claims.hypothesis: Why star formation is inefficient in the northern filaments
claims.experiment: Extract GMCs from ALMA CO(1-0) and derive their dynamical properties
claims.result: Virial parameters ~8-12, free-fall time about twice the dynamical time
claims.finding: Clouds are not gravitationally bound, which limits star formation

evidence.quote: Finally, we found that the free-fall time is about twice the dynamical time.

claims.hypothesis: Horseshoe complex differs from the rest of the filaments
claims.experiment: Compare CO with Halpha, FUV, clusters and MUSE BPT
claims.result: Horseshoe has Halpha but no FUV or clusters; shock excited
claims.finding: Two regimes: inefficient Horseshoe and star-forming Vertical filament

evidence.quote: The molecular clouds observed with ALMA seem to present two star formation regimes.

limitations_admitted.value: ALMA 12 m data recover only ~20% of APEX mass due to spatial filtering; narrow radius range limits Larson-relation tests

evidence.quote: the present data recover only 20% of the total molecular gas mass found by APEX.

referee_caveats_inferred: Cloud properties depend on clumpfind splitting of filtered emission
Constant alpha_CO=4.3 assumed in a jet-shocked environment
Short-spacing filtering biases sizes and virial parameters
